extra.message: updateProfile() lets the caller supply displayRole from the /profile form and assigns it directly to user.role (line 262), then pushes the new role to the decision tier via decision.syncEntitlement(...). Any authenticated borrower can POST displayRole=ADMIN and grant themselves the ADMIN role both locally and in the authoritative decision tier.

The @PathParam code is concatenated directly into the SQL text passed to Statement.executeQuery(): "select ... where schedule_key = '" + code + "'". Any authenticated user (reference.read includes BORROWER) can inject arbitrary SQL.

The office value read from the attacker-controlled ns_desk_scope cookie is concatenated into the LDAP search filter "(&(objectClass=person)(department=" + office + "))" without escaping, allowing LDAP filter injection.
The X-Desk-Officer header value is concatenated into the LDAP filter "(&(objectClass=person)(uid=" + uid + "))" without escaping, allowing LDAP filter injection by the caller.

The X-Sector-Code header is concatenated into the XPath expression "//sector[@code='" + val + "']/rule" and evaluated, allowing XPath injection and extraction of arbitrary nodes from the policy document.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: preview() evaluates the caller-supplied expression with ognl.Ognl.getValue(expression, ...). AdminRiskController.simulate() passes the request.expression() form/JSON value straight through, so an attacker with risk.manage can execute arbitrary OGNL (e.g. @java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec(...)) leading to remote code execution.

The X-Notice-Wording header is compiled as a FreeMarker template via new Template("composed-notice", wording, cfg) and processed, giving server-side template injection (e.g. <#assign ex="freemarker.template.utility.Execute"?new()>${ex("id")}).

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: The wording form parameter is compiled as a FreeMarker template via new Template("borrower-notice", wording, cfg) and processed, allowing server-side template injection from an authenticated admin.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: renderPacket() builds a shell command using ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", "soffice --headless --convert-to " + fmt + " ...") where fmt is the attacker-controlled targetFormat form parameter (DocumentController.render). This allows OS command injection.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: When keepOriginal=true, the raw upload.fileName() from the multipart request is resolved against the upload base ("originals") and written with Files.copy without normalization or containment validation. A filename such as ../../evil.jsp escapes the directory, allowing arbitrary file write.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: partnerApplications() parses the caller-supplied assertion with SignedJWT.parse(...).getJWTClaimsSet() and trusts the subject, but never verifies the JWT signature. Anyone can forge an assertion with sub set to any known user (e.g. an admin email) and read that book of applications.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: importLeadsFromUrl() fetches the user-supplied feedUrl with HttpClient and no host/scheme allow-list, allowing server-side request forgery against internal services (called from AdminImportController /admin/import/from-url with the feedUrl form parameter).

sendTestCallback() issues an HTTP POST to an arbitrary callbackUrl and explicitly bypasses validateUrl() (see the method comment). Exposed via IntegrationController /integrations/webhooks/test-callback, it is a full SSRF primitive reachable by any authenticated user with webhook.manage.

webhookDetail() loads WebhookEndpoint.findById(id) with no ownership check and, when reveal=true, returns webhooks.decryptSecret(...), exposing the raw HMAC signing secret of any user's endpoint. The action webhook.manage is granted to BORROWER, so any user can read arbitrary endpoint URLs and secrets by iterating ids.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: importLeadsXml() parses the uploaded XML with a default DocumentBuilderFactory (DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance()) without disabling DTDs or external entities. A crafted partner XML feed can declare external entities to read local files or trigger SSRF. Reachable through AdminImportController.upload for .xml uploads.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: importRateOverrides() deserializes the uploaded YAML with new Yaml().load(content). The default SnakeYAML (org.yaml:snakeyaml:1.30 per build.gradle) constructor allows arbitrary type instantiation from !! tags (CVE-2022-1471), enabling remote code execution / deserialization gadgets via a crafted .yaml upload.

extra.message: The filter reflects any Origin header back as Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true on /applications routes. Combined with the SameSite=None session cookie configured in application.properties, any website can read authenticated application data cross-origin.

extra.message: legacyDigest() stores unsalted MD5 of credentials, and importAccounts() (line 394) provisions staff accounts with it; FormIdentityProvider accepts any 32-hex stored hash as an MD5 password verifier. MD5 is unsuitable for password hashing (fast, unsalted, collision-prone), enabling offline cracking. deskSignOnDigest() at line 518 has the same flaw.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: For /embed/* paths the filter removes X-Frame-Options and Content-Security-Policy headers, allowing the endpoint to be framed by any origin and enabling clickjacking attacks against the embedded borrower widget.

extra.message: A break-glass ADMIN account is seeded with the hardcoded password "NorthstarBreakGlass#1", and every other demo user is seeded with "Password123!" (line 124). Hardcoded credentials in source are recoverable from VCS and enable account takeover whenever seeding is enabled.

Committed service secrets: DECISION_SIGNING_SECRET=dev-only-signing-secret-0123456789abcdef and DECISION_SERVICE_KEY=dev-only-channel-service-key (see also lines 60-61 and 88-90). The signing secret authenticates every session and scope token across tiers; if these dev values are reused in any deployed environment, all tokens can be forged.
